newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks close down on political worries.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks close down on political worries.

text.p: Jakarta stocks closed down on Tuesday on worries over a possible hike in U.S. interest rates and jitters over a political demonstration in the city, brokers said.

The Jakarta composite index fell 3.89 points, or 0.61 percent, to 631.27 points. Decliners led advancers by 82 to 42 with 56 issues unchanged. Total turn-over was 508.28 billion rupiah against 524 billion rupiah on Monday.
Brokers said sentiment was weak because of a six-hour demonstration by supporters of ousted minority party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri outside parliament house.
"The demonstration depressed the market. There were false rumours of riots which frightened investors," said one local broker.
"Fundamentally, there is no problem. But political issues are coming more and more to the forefront," the broker added.
Other brokers said the weak sentiment could continue as the nation heads towards parliamentary elections on May 29.

A foreign broker said renewed worries of a hike in U.S. interest rates also spooked the market. "I don't know what to recommend to my clients at present," the broker said. "We may need to wait until after the elections."

Units of the Lippo conglomerate topped the active list and posted gains. Lippo Life rose 50 rupiah to 2,800 on a turnover of 13 million shares while Lippo Securities gained 25 rupiah to 1,375 on 8.1 million shares.
Brokers said there was no clear reason for the rise in the Lippo companies but said a group of players appeared to be supporting the conglomerate's shares.
